transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble with... my face. 

There's this... this rough, sunken-looking patch. It just makes one side of me look all old and beat-up. I can't really stop seeing it whenever I look in the mirror, or if I see a photo of myself. 

People keep telling me they barely notice anything, but... yeah. I just can't stop seeing it. So I'm here.
Do you find yourself thinking about this patch on your face a lot during the day?

Yeah... I guess so. Like I was saying, I just can't really unsee it. 

If I walk by a mirror or... catch my reflection somewhere, it's just right there. Staring at me. It just makes that whole side of my face look so rough and beat-up, you know? So... yeah. It's on my mind a lot.
Is this concern about your face affecting your daily life or relationships in any way?

I guess... maybe a little. I mean, sometimes it takes me a while to get out the door in the mornings, so... I've been running late for my construction jobs. 

And... well, I usually duck out of the way if they're taking site photos now. I just don't really want to be in 'em. I've even been sitting out some family game nights lately. I just... I'd rather stay home than have everyone looking at my face, you know? It's just easier.
Is it always this particular patch on your face that bothers you, or are there other features that sometimes catch your attention as well?
No... just this one spot. I don't really pay attention to the rest of it. It's just... that patch.
Do you think this patch on your face is actually getting worse over time?
I don't really know. Maybe. It's... hard to tell, I guess. I just know it looks bad. I haven't really thought about if it's changing or not... it's just always there.
Is there anything that could potentially fix or improve the appearance of this patch on your face?
I don't know. I haven't really... I haven't thought about fixing it, I guess. I mean, what could you even do? It's just... it is what it is. I haven't looked into anything like that.
Do you think your life would go back to normal if this patch on your face were to suddenly disappear?
I don't know. ...Maybe. I haven't really thought about it like that. It's hard to say.
Is it the appearance of the patch itself that bothers you, or is it more about what you think others might think of it?
I don't really know. I guess I haven't broken it down like that. It just... it just bothers me. I don't really know about the rest of it.
Do you think people are judging you or noticing this patch on your face when you're around them?

I'm not sure. I mean, I guess it's possible, but... I don't really pay that much attention to what other people are doing. I just try to keep my head down and get through the day. I don't know if they're looking or not.
Do you think that others can see this patch on your face as clearly as you can?

I mean... people keep saying they barely notice anything. So, I guess not. But... I don't really get it, because I can't stop seeing it. Whenever I look in the mirror, or... or if I see a photo. It's just this rough, sunken-looking patch right there. It makes that whole side of my face look old and... beat-up. I don't know how they don't see it.
Is it the idea that others might see this patch on your face that bothers you the most?
I don't... I don't really know. Like I said, I don't pay much attention to other people. It's just... I see it. That's what bothers me. I don't really think about what other people are doing.
Is it the patch on your face itself that bothers you, or is it more about how you think it affects the way others see you?
I... I thought I just answered that. It's the patch itself. I don't really care how other people see me or what they think. It's just... looking at it myself. That's all it is.
Is there anything else about your appearance that you've ever been concerned about, or is it just this patch on your face?
No, just this. I don't really worry about the rest of it. Just... just the patch.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals in an attempt to cope with your concerns about the patch on your face?

I don't know about rituals. I wouldn't call it that. I just... before I head to the job site, or if I'm supposed to go to my sister's game night, I end up checking the bathroom mirror a lot. 

Just... turning my face under the different lights to see it. Sometimes I catch myself rubbing at the spot. If it looks too obvious to me, I'll just pull my hat down low... or I just make an excuse not to go at all. That's about it.
Do you feel like you have to check your face in the mirror, or is it something you just find yourself doing?
I guess... I just find myself doing it. I don't know if I *have* to. It's just... I walk by the mirror, and I look. That's all.
Do you feel like you can stop checking your face in the mirror if you want to?
I don't really know. I guess... I never really tried to just not look. Like I said, I just kind of do it. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when you can't check your face in the mirror?

I don't know about anxious. I don't really get like that. 

I mean... there's usually a bathroom around, or a truck mirror at the site. So I haven't really been in a spot where I couldn't look. I just... I haven't really noticed.
Do you feel like checking your face in the mirror is something you can control?
I don't know. Like I said, I just haven't really tried to stop. It's just a habit, I guess. I don't really think about controlling it.
Do you feel like something bad would happen if you didn't check your face in the mirror?
Something bad? No. I don't really... I don't know what you mean by that. It's not like the roof's gonna cave in or something. I just... I just look. That's all.
Do you feel like you're checking your face in the mirror to make sure it looks okay, or to make sure the patch isn't getting worse?
I don't really know. I guess I just... look at it. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just check it to see it, I guess. I'm not really thinking about it that deep.
